title: @MainActor & nonisolated
hints: `@MainActor` isolates a type to the main actor; outsiders must `await`.
Mark the helper `nonisolated static`; from `uiDemo`, await the initialiser, `load`, and reading `items`.
`let vm = await ViewModel(); await vm.load(names); let items = await vm.items`.
jsBridge: `@MainActor` pins code to the main thread, where UI must run, like everything in JS running on the UI thread. `nonisolated` opts a member out so pure helpers can run anywhere.

compass.q: In JS, everything is on the main thread, so heavy work blocks the UI. How does `@MainActor` + `nonisolated` let Swift split UI and work?
